anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Cardinality-estimation inputs are stale or incomplete, causing the optimizer to misestimate row counts and skew, and to choose sub-optimal plans and memory grants.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The database engine allocates or leaks more memory than the host can safely supply, provoking paging, cache churn, or OOM events.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes exhaust available CPU cycles, driving the host into sustained compute saturation.

When these three root causes co-exist, symptoms intermingle and intensify: execution plans show grossly inaccurate estimates, excessive hash and sort buffers, and over-parallelized operators; resident-set size and temp usage grow until the OS starts paging, while buffer-cache hit ratios and plan-cache health deteriorate; at the same time run-queue length, context switches, and scheduler wait events climb, and every query—good or bad—experiences sharp latency spikes. Memory pressure can also bounce processes in and out of the CPU, inflating both CPU usage and wait-for-CPU statistics, making it hard to distinguish whether slowness stems from compute, memory, or plan quality.

Causal chain: stale or missing statistics mislead the optimizer into selecting join orders, parallel degrees, and memory grants that demand far more work areas than the workload truly needs. These oversized allocations aggregate across sessions, tipping the instance into memory pressure; paging and cache eviction then inflate CPU time per I/O and per context switch. The elevated CPU consumption further slows statistics maintenance tasks and prolongs queries, perpetuating statistic staleness and keeping bad plans alive. In turn, CPU saturation limits throughput, causing sessions to linger and hold their large memory reservations even longer, closing a positive-feedback loop that degrades both throughput and stability until either resources are reclaimed or the instance fails.

entry.official_definition: Maximum wait for connection, in seconds; zero or not specified means wait indefinitely.
entry.trigger_condition: A libpq client connection attempt exceeds connect_timeout seconds.
entry.workload_impact: The client connection attempt fails instead of waiting indefinitely.
entry.default_behavior: Zero or absent value means wait indefinitely.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
